record.original_question: Can one construct a mechanical or fluid model whose configuration space is the group D_mu(M) of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms and whose energy metric is a left-invariant L2 metric? Are there physically interesting systems exhibiting that left invariance?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a compact Riemannian manifold (possibly with boundary) equipped with a volume form $\mu$, and let $D_\mu(M)$ denote the group of smooth volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$. For a vector field $u$ on $M$, define the $L^2$ inner product $\langle u,v\rangle_{L^2} = \int_M \langle u(x),v(x)\rangle_{g(x)}\,d\mu(x)$, where $g$ is the Riemannian metric on $M$. A Riemannian metric on $D_\mu(M)$ is called left-invariant if the left translations $L_\varphi:\eta\mapsto\varphi\circ\eta$ are isometries for every $\varphi\in D_\mu(M)$. (In contrast, the classical Arnold description of the Euler equations of an ideal incompressible fluid identifies the fluid motion with the geodesic flow on $D_\mu(M)$ for the right-invariant $L^2$ metric.)

Problem: Construct a mechanical or fluid-dynamical system whose configuration space is $D_\mu(M)$ and whose kinetic energy is given by a left-invariant $L^2$ metric on $D_\mu(M)$. Exhibit physically meaningful examples of such systems and describe the resulting Euler–Lagrange/geodesic equations, or else show that no such physically interesting model can exist.
artifact.status_search_result: The literature on Euler–Arnold theory consistently treats ideal fluid motion as geodesic flow for the right-invariant L² metric on the volume-preserving diffeomorphism group; left-invariant L² analogues appear in diffeomorphic image matching but no widely recognized physical fluid/mechanical model with left-invariant L² energy on D_μ(M) is reported. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Euler–Arnold equation - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Euler–Arnold equations describe geodesic flow on infinite-dimensional Lie groups equipped with right-invariant metrics.
status_evidence.claim: Standard hydrodynamic interpretation uses right-invariant, not left-invariant, metrics.

status_evidence.title: Diffeomorphic Image Matching with Left-Invariant Metrics
status_evidence.snippet: Left-invariant metrics on diffeomorphism groups have been explored, based on reproducing kernels in body coordinates.
status_evidence.claim: Left-invariant metrics on diffeomorphism groups have been studied in image-matching contexts, but not as physical fluid models.

status_evidence.title: Semi-invariant Riemannian metrics in hydrodynamics
status_evidence.snippet: New difficulties arise from the dependence of the inertia operator A(ρ) on the volume density ρ.
status_evidence.claim: Non-right-invariant metrics on diffeomorphism groups in hydrodynamics are still actively investigated.
